title: GraphRun
description: The durable record of a graph run (ADR-0008). This is the authoritative state: the HTTP call that dispatches a node attempt is an optimisation, not the record (ADR-0004 §7). Only the holder of the lease may transition a run.

schemaVersion.description: ADR-0024 §5: stored documents are versioned as data. One version exists in V1.

version.description: Optimistic concurrency token. Every write is guarded by both the expected version and a lease check (ADR-0008 §9).

graphVersionHash.description: Pinned at creation (ADR-0008 §2). Publishing a new definition never affects an in-flight run; there is no in-flight migration.

agentPins.description: agentId to agentVersionHash, resolved exactly once at run creation (ADR-0022 §3) in the same durable write that pins graphVersionHash. From that instant the run uses these versions for every attempt, retry and resume, including after a week-long approval pause. Without this the graph pins only the agent's name, so editing an agent changes the behaviour of in-flight runs of an already-pinned graph.

status.description: ADR-0008 §6. SUSPENDED is the normal consequence of closing a laptop — an expected, recoverable state, not a failure. Terminal states are immutable.

epoch.description: Bumped on lease takeover and on cancellation. Lets a stale orchestrator detect that it no longer speaks for this run.

lease.description: ADR-0008 §8: exactly one orchestrator per run. This is a security control as well as a correctness one, because two orchestrators would produce duplicate external side effects.

workItemRef.description: The Jira issue this run serves, where there is one. Jira remains the system of record; this is a reference, not a copy.

cancellationRequested.description: ADR-0008 §14. Cancellation always stops new work and is best-effort for work in flight. Stated plainly because the opposite is routinely assumed.

currency.description: ADR-0026 §1. ISO 4217 code, fixed for the run's lifetime. A run whose model policy could resolve to providers billing in different currencies is rejected at creation (§2): the platform does not convert, because a converted budget is enforced against an exchange rate nobody recorded.

budget.description: ADR-0026 §3. The run ceiling, and the only budget that is mandatory. Node and grant budgets are optional and are clamped to what remains here, so the nesting is genuine containment rather than four independent numbers.

consumedCostUnits.description: ADR-0026 §4. Monotonically non-decreasing, updated in the same transactional batch as the ModelResponse or ToolResult that incurred the cost. A separate update can be lost, and lost spend is spend the platform believes did not happen. Failed attempts accumulate: forgiving them under-counts exactly the runs that are going wrong.

approvalDeadline.description: ADR-0025 §3. Once passed, APPROVAL_EXPIRED stops being retryable regardless of remaining attempt budget. This is the bound that stops a forgotten run re-requesting approval indefinitely while holding a workspace lease.

initiatedBy.description: The local developer who started the run. Self-asserted in V1 (ADR-0016 §4); the platform records what it can honestly attest to and no more.
